subject: Post-call: latency vs cost — pricing bands and SLO-driven options
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — latency vs cost (token bands)

Hi Raj — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the asks I captured so we have alignment: 

- Use case: clinical-summarization assistant for internal care coordinators (short responses, ~120-250 tokens generated per call).
- QPS profile: peak ~40 rps during morning hours, baseline ~8 rps.
- Average input tokens per request: ~90 tokens (user prompt + metadata).
- Target SLOs: 95th pctl latency <= 350ms for interactive flows; some lower-priority batch jobs can tolerate up to 2s.
- Budget guidance: looking to validate economics at ~target $/1M tokens in the $650-$1,100 range (they asked for a tight unit-economics check).

Immediate asks from your team: 
1) A short cost model (per 1M tokens) showing tradeoffs between Hosted Standard vs Hosted LowCost tiers, with/without streaming and batching.
2) Recommended config to meet the 95th pctl <=350ms SLO and an alternative low-cost option that meets 95th <=700ms.
3) Any constraints for data residency and SOC2 artifacts — procurement will request evidence if we move to SOW.

Next steps I suggest: I will send a short cost matrix and two recommended deployment profiles (SLO-prioritized and cost-prioritized). Ava will validate latency numbers and provide suggested batching/streaming knob values. Lauren — looping you for pricing guardrails for discounts/commits if we move to Dedicated.

Attached: token_estimate_breakdown.csv (simple traffic scenarios).

Want to confirm timeline: can we get you the cost matrix and config options by EOD Friday (8/14)?

Thanks,
--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@brightedgehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightedgehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-12T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency vs cost (token bands)

Thanks Priyom — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from procurement before you build the matrix: 

- For the $/1M token target: the $650 number is aggressive but represents our ideal threshold. $1,100 is our stretch maximum for hosted, beyond which we will require a committed Dedicated price.
- Traffic skew: the morning spike is the main concern. Approximately 60% of daily traffic occurs between 08:00-11:00 local. 
- Feature flags: we will consider streaming for the live agent UI only; backend batch jobs do not need streaming.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required. We have an existing approved vendor list; Redwood is not yet on it — procurement will need SOC2 report and a short security questionnaire (I’ll attach in a follow-up).

Confirming EOD Friday is fine. If you can show a configuration that hits <=350ms at 95p for our interactive traffic at or below $900/1M tokens, we’ll be very interested to run a short pilot.

-Raj
Director of Product, BrightEdge Health
raj.patel@brightedgehealth.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: cost/latency options for BEH (see Raj notes)

Ava / Lauren — forwarding Raj's clarifications below. Key asks: 95p <=350ms at or below $900/1M tokens would be ideal for them. 

Quoted: 
> 
> "If you can show a configuration that hits <=350ms at 95p for our interactive traffic at or below $900/1M tokens, we’ll be very interested to run a short pilot."

Ava: can you validate the feasibility and give two concrete profiles we can present: 
- Profile A (SLO-first): streaming enabled, Hosted Standard tier (higher-perf GPU selection), batch_size small (continuous batching with max latency budget 40ms), prewarming KV cache for common prefixes — target 95p <=350ms.
- Profile B (Cost-first): no streaming for most calls, Hosted LowCost tier (quantized model variant), larger batching window (50-80ms), aggressive prefix cache and response truncation for long tails — target 95p <=700ms, cost optimized.

Please include estimated $/1M tokens for each profile assuming their traffic mix (use token_estimate_breakdown.csv attached to the thread). Lauren: flag any discount thresholds (commits) that would move the unit price into sub-$900 territory and typical lead times for Dedicated discussions.

Ava — rough numbers are fine (ballpark per-million token and expected 95p latencies under the load profile). I’ll fold into a short customer-facing note.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@brightedgehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-14T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing + configuration options (SLO-first and cost-first) — BrightEdge Health pilot path

Hi Raj — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our commitments, attached a compact cost matrix and recommended deployment profiles. High-level summary first: 

1) Profile A — SLO-first (Interactive priority)- Expected 95p latency: ~320ms- Key settings: Hosted Standard tier, streaming ON for interactive UI, continuous batching with 20-30ms batching window, KV cache prewarm for top-200 prompts- Estimated unit cost: ~$870 / 1M tokens (based on their morning spike distribution + our continuous batching assumptions)- Notes: Best-fit if the 95p <=350ms requirement is non-negotiable.

2) Profile B — Cost-first (mixed workloads)- Expected 95p latency: ~580-700ms (variance during peak)- Key settings: Hosted LowCost tier, streaming OFF (use chunked responses for long outputs), batching window 60-80ms, aggressive model quantization (8-bit)- Estimated unit cost: ~$560 / 1M tokens- Notes: Good platform test to validate unit economics before committing; some conversational UX degradation on tail latencies.

3) Hybrid approach (recommended pilot): Start with Profile A for the interactive UI during pilot hours (08:00-12:00) and Profile B for non-interactive/background jobs. This lets you validate UX while keeping overall blended unit cost near $720 / 1M tokens for initial traffic mix.

Commercial guardrails / procurement notes (Lauren): 
- To reach <$650 / 1M tokens we typically need a 12-month Dedicated commit (TBD size).
- Early pilot credits and a short-term commit (3 months, modest min) can bring the effective pilot cost down ~10% for them.
- SOC2 Type II report and security questionnaire link: Lauren has approved package we can push if procurement confirms interest.

Attachments: token_estimate_breakdown.csv (detailed scenarios), redwood_pricing_bands_v1.pdf (banded pricing and units), mini_sow_draft.docx (starter language).

If this looks good I propose: 
- Action 1: Raj/procurement confirms pilot acceptance + any required PO/compliance docs by 8/18.
- Action 2: Redwood sets up a short performance run (3 business days) configured as Profile A for 08:00-12:00 and Profile B otherwise; we’ll capture 95p latency and tokens consumed.
- Action 3: Post-run review with AJ from BEH and our SREs; then iterate on commit sizing.

Would you like us to prepare a one-page pilot SOW and a DocuSign link? If yes, we can send a mini-SOW (attached) and a DocuSign by EOD Monday.

Thanks — feel free to call if you want to talk through the numbers.

Best,
--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
